name: Factory Droid

surfaces.label: Factory App (Electron desktop app, Homebrew cask `factory`, /Applications/Factory.app). Deliberately no process rule: the Electron host and its Chromium helpers would always look busy, and what process runs the agent inside the app (a `droid` child, a `droid daemon`, or in-process) is not documented. Bundle id is inferred from the cask zap list (Preferences/ai.factory.desktop.plist), never read from an Info.plist. Any `droid` process the app starts is caught by the daemon or exec surfaces below.
Editor ACP client (Zed extension, JetBrains AI Agents): the editor spawns `droid exec --output-format acp`. Parent is the editor, not a TUI.
`droid daemon [--remote-access]`: the Factory daemon (SDK example URL ws://127.0.0.1:37643). Hosts many sessions and can run turns concurrently, so its CPU cannot be attributed to one session.

`droid exec`: headless run. Spawned by CI, scripts, the Python/TypeScript SDK (`droid exec --input-format stream-jsonrpc --output-format stream-jsonrpc`), and, per a third-party read of the 0.218.2 bundle, as the agent-loop child of every interactive TUI. The probe keeps the outermost match, so the TUI wins when there is one.

`droid` interactive terminal UI (also `droid resume`, `droid "prompt"`). Native single-file Bun binary named `droid`, installed to ~/.local/bin/droid by the installer, or linked into $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/bin by the cask. Matched by executable name only (plus the anchored /Caskroom/droid/ path): a bare path_contains of /.local/bin/droid is a substring test and also matched /.local/bin/droidcam and /.local/bin/droid-helper, so it was removed. `npm install -g droid` may run through a `node .../bin/droid` shim (npm package bin/droid is a node script unless postinstall hard-links the binary); the shim is not matched, its native `droid` child is. A fresh session has NO id in argv (only a hook reveals it); resumed ones carry it after `--resume`/`-r`/`resume`.
Droid Computers (Factory-managed), Slack/Linear/Jira remote delegations, GitHub droid-action, Factory web. No local process; BYOM machines run `droid daemon --remote-access` locally.

working_signals.meaning: Newest write to <session>.jsonl (message and compaction_state records). The sibling <session>.settings.json (rewritten during the session with tokenUsage) may also move, but tools/agents_probe.py only stats the per_session .jsonl, so a detector that wants the settings file must add it itself; whether it ticks during a turn is unverified. Window is inferred, not measured: no live instance was available, and Codex-style mid-turn gaps (long model calls, long tools) are likely. Cannot be used for a fresh TUI whose id is not in argv.
CPU of the droid process tree (TUI plus its agent-loop child). Floor is a guess above Claude Code's 3 because the TUI may animate while idle; unmeasured.

Missions only: the CLI holds an idle-sleep inhibitor while a Mission runs (keepSystemAwakeDuringMissions, default true), and the Factory App has a keep-awake setting for agent runs. Assertion name is unverified. There is no general per-turn assertion, so a missing assertion never means idle.

waiting_signals.meaning: Droid is waiting for permission to run tool(s). No request id or options in the payload.
Droid is asking the user structured question(s), from the AskUser tool.

Docs: waiting for user input, including right after the user cancels a turn. Third-party bundle read: fires only after a user interrupt, no timed idle notification. Interrupt does NOT fire Stop, so this is the only hook that closes an interrupted turn.

droid_working_state_changed newState, plus droid.request_permission and droid.ask_user requests. Only visible to the process that owns a `droid exec` stream (an SDK client); an external observer cannot see it.

waiting_signals.record: assistant tool_use named AskUser with no later tool_result
waiting_signals.meaning: Inferred from a third-party read of the session schema; unverified on a live file.

hooks.config: ~/.factory/hooks.json (user), .factory/hooks.json (project), or a top-level `hooks` key in the matching ~/.factory/settings.json / .factory/settings.json (the hooks docs name only settings.json; a settings.local.json `hooks` key is inferred from the settings merge hierarchy, not documented); org-managed settings (allowManagedHooksOnly); plugin hooks/hooks.json; legacy .factory/hooks/hooks.json; `--settings <path>` for one process; manage with /hooks; disable all with hooksDisabled

telemetry.how: OTLP over HTTP, metrics only by default, to {endpoint}/v1/metrics. Set OTEL_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT (falls back to OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT) and OTEL_TELEMETRY_HEADERS in the environment, or pin a `telemetry` block in org-managed settings (org wins; ignored in user/project settings). Spans (droid.message.*, droid.tool.* or gen_ai.* with OTEL_TELEMETRY_FORMAT=genai) exist only with a customer collector and OTEL_LOG_MESSAGE_CONTENT=true. In connected deployments metrics also go to Factory's own collector. Metrics use delta temporality, 60 s flush. No logs signal documented. Not a live working/idle signal: it needs a collector and lags by the flush interval.

sources.evidence: python3 driving agents_probe.matches over the row: `droid`, `droid --resume x`, `droid resume x`, `droid exec -s x`, ACP, daemon, Caskroom path -> intended surface; `droid update`, `droid doctor`, `droid --version`, Factory.app binary, `node .../bin/droid` -> no match; BEFORE repair `/Users/x/.local/bin/droidcam` and `/Users/x/.local/bin/droid-helper` -> tui (false positive, fixed); still matches by design of the substring rule: `droid execute the plan` -> exec surface, `droid explain the daemon design` -> daemon surface, `droid fix the search bug` -> no match (missed TUI)

notes: No live instance was available, so no process, path or signal here was seen running. Read this row with these gotchas. (1) Per a third-party read of the 0.218.2 bundle, every interactive TUI has a persistent `droid exec` child (older builds spawned a daemon per TUI per the changelog; either child is dropped by the probe's outermost-match rule), so tool_children and child counts are expected to be non-zero: that is why tool_children is NOT a working signal here. Unverified on a live process. tree_cpu on the outer `droid` covers the child. (2) A fresh TUI has no session id in argv; map it to a transcript by the hook's session_id/transcript_path or by cwd plus newest mtime under ~/.factory/sessions/<cwd slug>/. (3) The hooks docs example shows transcript_path under ~/.factory/projects/..., while SDK source and a bundle read show ~/.factory/sessions/; the hook's transcript_path is the only pointer Factory publishes, so prefer it and fall back to the glob. Some third-party tools also scan ~/.factory/projects/<slug>/. (4) The probe splits args on spaces and args_contain is a SUBSTRING test, so any prompt word containing `exec` (execute, executor) or `daemon` (daemonize) misroutes an interactive TUI to the exec or daemon surface (session_id_args then read -s instead of --resume; the daemon surface reports kind daemon), and a prompt word exactly equal to an excluded subcommand (search, find, update, mcp, rules, computer, plugin, doctor) drops a live TUI from detection because exclude_args is an exact-element test. Most TUIs are launched without a prompt, so this is rare; it cannot be fixed in the row without changing the probe. Zed also runs its own downloaded `./droid` (pinned old CLI, so its architecture may differ). `-r` means --resume in the TUI but --reasoning-effort in exec. (5) The most precise turn signal is hook-based (UserPromptSubmit opens, Stop or Notification idle_prompt closes) or the stream-jsonrpc working state for a process you own; neither needs a live probe of CPU but both need user configuration or ownership. (6) `droid --resume` with no id returns no session; `--fork <id>` is not a session-id flag because it creates a new id.
